title: House okays bill lowering gov't workers' retirement age to 56
summary: A bill seeking to lower the optional retirement age of government employees from 60 to 56 has been approved on third and final reading in the House of Representatives.

blocks.text: A bill seeking to lower the retirement age of government employees from 60 to 56 has been approved on third and final reading in the House of Representatives.
House Bill No. 10995 received 209 affirmative votes, no objections and one abstention during the plenary session on Tuesday.
Among the authors of the measure were Speaker Faustino "Bojie" Dy III of Isabela and House Majority Leader Ferdinand Alexander "Sandro" Marcos of Ilocos Norte.

The bill seeks to amend Section 13-A of Republic Act No. 8291, or the Government Service Insurance System (GSIS) Act of 1997, by allowing GSIS members to retire at age 56, provided they have rendered at least 15 years of service and are not receiving a monthly pension due to permanent total disability.
Qualified retiring members would receive their corresponding retirement benefits from the GSIS.

The authors said the proposed measure would give qualified personnel among the more than one million government workers the option to retire early and spend more years with their families using their retirement benefits and savings.
They also said the measure would allow retirees to pursue other passions or explore opportunities in other fields while opening up positions for younger government personnel.— MCG, GMA News
